name: Expansion whitespace review
summary: For one account or a whole book, the account manager sees what each customer holds against what it could also use, the evidence for every gap, the plays ranked, and one next step and owner for each. A person decides what to propose; nothing goes into the sales system without approval.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own rules for prepared work: the organization's own catalogue and settings as the only authority, evidence graded and quoted with its source, every next step with one owner and one due date, and a person who decides, approves and creates every record.

sources.contribution: The method this template adapts: one account in depth or a sweep of a book; what a customer has set against what it could add across products, teams, locations and volume; a gap counted only with evidence; plays ranked on evidence, size drawn from the seller's own usual values and how well the seller knows the people involved; an approach building on an existing success; unsupported items kept apart with the signal that would raise them; the best play per account in a book view; opportunity records proposed with evidence and created only on a person's acceptance; working from uploaded exports.

The usual expansion signals (usage nearing a limit, a request only a higher tier answers, people joining the customer's team, a new need raised in a review), the kinds of play (more seats, higher tier, a further product, wider rollout), waiting until a new customer has had value from onboarding before raising expansion, and keeping the customer before growing the account, so an account at risk comes before any upsell.
